title: Nessa and the Rainbow Ears
markdown:
Nessa, a young ogre with skin the soft green of mossy stones, loved her evening strolls. The sun, like a sleepy warm berry, was sinking low, painting the sky soft apricot and pink. Her favourite place was the whispering pine woods. Tall trees shared secrets with the wind, and the air smelled fresh and piney. It was a time for gentle joy.

As Nessa padded along on her big soft feet, she saw something tucked by a sturdy oak tree’s roots. It was a hat basket. At first it looked dusty and empty. But Nessa, always curious, tiptoed closer.

Her bright eyes blinked. The basket wasn’t empty. Curled up, fast asleep, was the most wondrous little creature. It was no bigger than her curled thumb. Its fur was white and soft, like a dandelion puff floating on the breeze. And its ears. Oh, its ears were long and wiggled, and they shimmered with rainbow colours. While it slept, it made sweet soft sounds, like a sleepy stream. A warm feeling bloomed in Nessa’s chest.

“Oh, my,” whispered Nessa. “Who left you here all alone?” She looked around, but saw only the quiet watching trees. The little creature twitched its nose, its rainbow ears wiggling in its sleep. Nessa felt a happy flutter, not of worry, but of gentle wonder.

With a soft mossy finger, Nessa reached out. The creature stirred. One rainbow ear unfurled like a tiny flag. It opened its eyes, like two dewdrops reflecting the sky. It didn’t look scared. It blinked and gave a tiny happy squeak. Nessa giggled, a soft sound like pebbles rolling in a clear stream. “You’re a Pipkin,” she declared. “A Pipkin the Puff-Bunny.” Pipkin wiggled his whole fluffy body. Nessa knew he liked his name.

But who did this sweet Pipkin belong to? He looked like he’d had a very, very long nap. Maybe he was lost. Nessa carefully picked up the basket. Pipkin snuggled back down, his rainbow ears drooping like sleepy flower petals.

Just then a sound drifted through the trees: squeak-squonk, squeak-squonk. That was Wizard Wobbly-Knees. His boots always sounded funny. He shuffled into the clearing, his sparkly beard almost catching on a branch. “Who’s there?” he called, his voice warm and reedy.

Nessa held up the basket, a hopeful smile on her face. “It’s me, Nessa. And look.” Pipkin poked his fluffy head out, blinking his dewdroppy eyes.

Wizard Wobbly-Knees peered over his glasses. His eyes twinkled. “Hooray,” he said, his boots giving an extra happy squonk. “That’s a Pipkin the Puff-Bunny. And that basket… ah, yes. That belongs to Beatrice Bumble, the bee-keeper from Sunny Meadow. She leaves her Pipkins for naps while she gathers nectar. She must have forgotten it.”

Nessa’s heart felt as light as a feather. A big ogre smile spread across her face. “Oh, that’s wonderful. So Pipkin isn’t lost?”

“Not even a little bit,” chuckled Wizard Wobbly-Knees, his beard wiggling. “Just enjoying a long snooze. Beatrice will be happy to see him safe. And you, Nessa, have been so kind and gentle looking after him.”

Nessa felt a lovely warm glow. She had helped. Pipkin gave a happy wiggle, and his rainbow ears seemed to shine brighter, like tiny captured sunbeams. Soon Beatrice Bumble arrived, her busy bees buzzing happily. Her face lit up like fireflies when she saw Pipkin. “Oh, my precious cloud-bunny,” she buzzed, giving Nessa a gentle hug that smelled of wildflowers.

As Nessa watched Beatrice and Pipkin trot happily towards Sunny Meadow, the pine woods felt even softer, and the evening air sweeter. The first stars began to peek out, like tiny happy eyes twinkling goodnight. Nessa finished her stroll the long way home, her big soft feet extra careful around any other baskets, just in case another puff-bunny was still mid-nap.
audience: children aged 5-6, story time at home
